tagline: Iron country to Amish country on two lanes.
intro: The byway sets out on PA 419 at Quentin, where it meets PA 72, and heads east through Cornwall, then turns northeast on Schaeffer Road into the farm country of southeastern Lebanon County, home to an Amish community. It is two lanes the whole way.

At Schaefferstown, settled before 1725 and at least a century older than the county around it, the road runs with PA 897 along Heidelberg Avenue before turning north on North Market Street. Then it is farmland again, through Millbach and down Main Street in Newmanstown to the Berks County line.

moments.title: Quentin
moments.text: The village was Bismark until October 1920, when it took the name of Quentin Roosevelt, Theodore Roosevelt's youngest son, killed flying as a fighter pilot in the First World War.

moments.title: Cornwall Iron Furnace
moments.text: Peter Grubb started the furnace in 1742 where the ore lay at or near the surface, and it is the only intact charcoal blast furnace on its original plantation in the Western Hemisphere.

moments.title: Schaefferstown
moments.text: Fountain Park in town is the oldest chartered waterworks still in operation in the United States.
